analysis:
The supplied units are BASE-side text excerpts (lines 1209-2033) of docs/architecture/inference.md; the PR is documentation-only (a date bump plus prose changes). The patch excerpt shows head changes at lines 684-691, 818-821 and 884-903, and the head 1740-1759 range falls in the supplied BASE region. No code is changed in the supplied evidence. The excerpts I could inspect do not change a control.

The patch adds prose saying GLM5Next's manifest aggregate is published as the weight hash, replacing separate pre-load and post-load WeightHasher passes. The next coordinator-mode start registers that hash without reading the weights while every file's device, inode, size, mtime and ctime are unchanged (VerifiedWeightHashStore). The load verifies again before serving. This touches T-012 (operator weight replacement), T-027 (weight-hash fail-open) and A-004. The security-relevant questions are about the underlying code and are not answered by the docs:
- Whether stat-metadata equality is a sufficient freshness proof against an operator who modifies file content while preserving size and mtime. ctime cannot be set by an ordinary user, so the document's claim is plausible.
- Whether the re-verification at load actually blocks serving on mismatch.
The code for VerifiedWeightHashStore, GLM5NextManagedLoad and ProviderLoop.verifiedGLM5NextWeightHash is not in the supplied evidence, so no regression can be claimed, and the next pass should review those source files. Because the supplied evidence is limited to documentation, I set needs_deeper_review=true for that code.

The BASE text I examined (prefill geometry, deadline admission, MTP, sampling, reasoning parsers, vision caps, MiMo) describes existing behavior. T-041 (prefix cache) is untouched by these ranges. The video-frame timing prose at 818-821 is a doc change on decode semantics and has no visible security impact.
